questions.questionMd: How does the lecture define a **port** in the context of computer networking?

options.text: A logical (as opposed to physical) connection point represented by a number ranging from 0 to 65535.
The unique IP address assigned to a server machine that allows it to be identified on the public internet.
An encrypted channel created by the operating system to secure all incoming TCP connections on a given server machine.
A physical socket on a server's network card used to plug in Ethernet cables and establish wired network connections.

questions.explanationMd: A network port is a logical endpoint identified by a number. It helps direct incoming network traffic to the correct service or process on a host.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following best describes **NodeJS**?

options.text: A JavaScript runtime written in C++ that can interpret and execute JavaScript and includes support for the NodeJS API.
A cloud-based execution environment that runs JavaScript on virtual machines and streams results back to the client browser.
A browser extension written in Python that allows JavaScript code to be executed outside the standard web browser environment.
A compiled language runtime that converts JavaScript source code into machine code and bundles it with DOM API libraries.

questions.explanationMd: NodeJS is a JavaScript runtime built on the V8 engine. It lets JavaScript run outside the browser and provides APIs for server-side and general-purpose programming.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, can **NodeJS** be used for purposes other than building web servers?

options.text: No, NodeJS requires an active internet connection at all times and cannot run JavaScript files that make no network requests.
No, NodeJS is exclusively designed for server-side HTTP handling and cannot execute scripts that do not involve network connections.
Yes, NodeJS can be used to write general-purpose JavaScript scripts that are completely unrelated to web servers.
Yes, but only if the scripts use the DOM API, because NodeJS was designed as a bridge between browser JavaScript and server JavaScript.

questions.explanationMd: NodeJS is not limited to web servers. It can run ordinary JavaScript programs, command-line tools, automation scripts, and other non-web-server code.

questions.questionMd: The lecture notes describe the term **server** as overloaded. What does this mean?

options.text: The word "server" refers to both the DNS resolution step and the TCP handshake step that occur before any data is transferred.
The word "server" can refer either to the physical machine running server software or to the software program itself, depending on context.
The word "server" simultaneously describes the TCP protocol layer and the HTTP application layer in a network stack.
The word "server" is used interchangeably with "client" in modern web development because both run JavaScript code.

questions.explanationMd: An overloaded term has more than one related meaning. In web development, **server** may mean the hardware machine or the server software running on that machine.

questions.questionMd: What does calling `server.listen(3000)` do in a NodeJS HTTP server program?

options.text: It creates a new TCP socket on port 3000, encrypts it with TLS, and then begins forwarding HTTPS traffic to the server handler.
It makes the program start accepting incoming HTTP messages sent to port 3000, keeping the process running indefinitely.
It imports the port 3000 configuration from the operating system's network settings and applies it to the current process.
It sends a test HTTP request to port 3000 to verify that no other server process is already occupying that port number.

questions.explanationMd: `server.listen(3000)` tells the NodeJS server to listen for incoming requests on port 3000. The process remains active so it can continue receiving requests.

questions.questionMd: In the context of networking, what is a **socket**?

options.text: A numbered logical endpoint, ranging from 0 to 65535, that identifies a specific service running on a host machine.
A physical hardware port on a server machine used to connect network cables to the motherboard.
The encrypted tunnel created by HTTPS to protect data exchanged between a client browser and a remote web server.
One end of a communication channel through which data can be sent and received.

questions.explanationMd: A socket represents one endpoint of a network communication channel. Data can be sent and received through that endpoint.

questions.questionMd: What is **npm** primarily used for in a NodeJS development workflow?

options.text: It is a command-line tool that installs packages (libraries and tools) written in JavaScript and compatible with NodeJS.
It is a browser extension that allows developers to inspect and modify the DOM of pages served from a NodeJS backend.
It is a version control system integrated with NodeJS that tracks changes to JavaScript source files across a development team.
It is a built-in NodeJS module that provides methods for creating HTTP servers and handling incoming TCP connections.

questions.explanationMd: npm is the Node package manager. It is commonly used from the command line to install and manage JavaScript packages for NodeJS projects.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what does **TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)** define?

options.text: The encryption standard applied to HTTPS traffic to protect data transmitted between clients and servers.
The structure and syntax of HTTP request and response messages exchanged between a browser and a web server.
The mapping between domain names and IP addresses maintained by distributed name servers across the internet.
The data format used for sending information over the network wire, and it can be used for HTTP, FTP, and other protocols.

questions.explanationMd: TCP is a transport-layer protocol used to send data reliably between endpoints. Application protocols such as HTTP and FTP can run over TCP.

questions.questionMd: When using the browser's `fetch()` API to send an HTTP **POST** request to `/hello`, which option correctly specifies the HTTP method?

options.text: `fetch('/hello', 'POST')`, passing the HTTP method as the second positional argument directly to the fetch function call.
`fetch('/hello', { method: 'POST' })`, passing an options object with the `method` property set to `'POST'`.
`fetch.post('/hello')`, which is a shorthand helper method on the fetch object specifically designed for POST requests.
`fetch('/hello', { type: 'POST' })`, where the `type` property in the options object overrides the default GET method.

questions.explanationMd: The `fetch()` function accepts an options object as its second argument. Setting `method: 'POST'` changes the HTTP method from the default GET to POST.

questions.questionMd: In a NodeJS HTTP request handler, what does calling `res.end()` do?

options.text: It writes the final message to the response body and signals to the server that the response is complete.
It terminates the NodeJS process and releases all bound ports back to the operating system's port pool.
It sets the HTTP status code of the response to 200 and automatically adds the Content-Type header to the message.
It closes the TCP connection and stops the server from listening for any further incoming HTTP requests on that port.

questions.explanationMd: `res.end()` finishes the HTTP response. It can send the final response data and tells NodeJS that no more response body will be written.

questions.questionMd: What is the purpose of the `require()` statement in NodeJS?

options.text: It loads a module into the current file, similar to `import` in Java or `include` in C++.
It instructs the V8 engine to pre-compile a JavaScript file into bytecode and cache it for faster future execution.
It sends an HTTP GET request to the npm registry to check whether a package is compatible with the current NodeJS version.
It declares a global variable that is shared across all JavaScript files in the same NodeJS project directory.

questions.explanationMd: `require()` is used in CommonJS-style NodeJS code to load modules, libraries, or local files into the current file.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what is the default port number used for **HTTP** requests when no port is specified in a URL?

options.text: Port 3000, which is the standard development port used by NodeJS and ExpressJS applications running locally.
Port 443, which is commonly reserved for encrypted HTTPS communication between browsers and remote web servers.
Port 53, which is assigned to the Domain Name System service for resolving hostnames to IP addresses.
Port 80, which is the well-known default port for Hypertext Transfer Protocol traffic on the World Wide Web.

questions.explanationMd: The default port for ordinary HTTP traffic is port 80. HTTPS commonly uses port 443, while 3000 is often used for local development.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture summary, after the server software receives an HTTP request, what is the correct sequence of actions it takes?

options.text: The server software binds to a new port, sends an HTTP GET request back to the client to confirm receipt, then closes the connection.
The server software parses the message, creates an HTTP response, and then the server OS sends that response to the client over TCP.
The server software immediately sends an empty 200 OK response and then asynchronously processes the request body in the background.
The server software forwards the raw TCP packet to the DNS server, which translates it and routes the reply back to the client browser.

questions.explanationMd: A typical server receives and parses an HTTP request, creates the appropriate HTTP response, and sends that response back to the client using the underlying TCP connection.

options.text: When a GET request is made to the path `/hello`, the server responds with the text `GET hello!`.
When any HTTP request arrives at the server, the response body is set to `GET hello!` regardless of the requested path.
When a POST request is made to the path `/hello`, the server replies with `GET hello!` to acknowledge receipt of the data.
When the server starts listening, it sends an HTTP GET request to the `/hello` endpoint to verify that the route is reachable.

questions.explanationMd: `app.get('/hello', ...)` registers a route handler for GET requests to `/hello`. The handler sends the response text `GET hello!`.

questions.subtopic: Raw NodeJS HTTP API vs ExpressJS
questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, why do developers prefer using **ExpressJS** over the raw NodeJS HTTP API for building servers?

options.text: The raw NodeJS HTTP APIs do not support JavaScript and instead require developers to write server logic in C++ directly.
The raw NodeJS HTTP APIs are low-level, requiring developers to manually parse requests, write responses, and handle a lot of tedious processing code.
The raw NodeJS HTTP APIs can only handle GET requests, so ExpressJS is required to support POST, PUT, and DELETE methods.
The raw NodeJS HTTP APIs are deprecated and no longer maintained, making ExpressJS the only officially supported way to build servers.

questions.explanationMd: ExpressJS provides higher-level routing and response helpers. This reduces the manual, low-level work required when using the raw NodeJS HTTP API directly.
